exposure: Women with a history of depression or anxiety
selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) use in the postpartum period
outcome: Positive postpartum depression screen (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale score ≥ 10 or > 0 on question 10)
cohort: 1237 women with private health insurance who gave birth at a single MFM practice between April 2015 and September 2016
finding: In a cohort of women with private health insurance, risk factors for a positive postpartum depression screen included nulliparity, cesarean delivery, non-White race, and a history of depression or anxiety.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk of a positive screen for postpartum depression.
